channel.title: Jaze — Security Research Feed
channel.description: Vulnerability research publications, advisories, and technical security analysis by Jaze.

item.title: 19 XSS in 24 Hours: Notes on Source Tracing, Sinks, and Framework Blindspots
item.description: A 24-hour sprint through the WordPress plugin repository revealed an eerie pattern: modern Gutenberg hydration and React DOM bridges repeatedly fall into the exact same architectural traps.

item.title: The Ghost Delete: How a Flawed Review Parameter Led to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Post Deletion
item.description: A look beyond obvious code execution sinks: how trusting client-supplied IDs in WooCommerce photo reviews turned WordPress comment cleanup into an unauthenticated database wipe.

item.title: My First Critical: How an Insecure Form Framework Led to Unauthenticated RCE in Tailored Tools
item.description: After hitting a string of duplicate reports, a late-night audit of a developer form framework uncovered raw file moves with zero checks — scoring a 9.0 Critical CVE.

item.title: Breaking Down CVE-2026-115607: An Unauthenticated UNION SQLi in WordPress DXP ToolKit
item.description: A commented-out authentication check combined with raw string concatenation turned a REST API search parameter into an instant, in-band database dump.

item.title: I Bricked My ESP32-S3 With My Own CTF Challenge (And How eFuse Parity Saved Me)
item.description: What happens when a security researcher builds a hardware CTF challenge with ESP32-S3 flash encryption and inadvertently turns their only dev board into a hardened cryptographic paperweight? A humorous post-mortem on eFuses, JTAG lockouts, and the quirky odd-even counter trick that brought it back from the dead.

item.title: V1T CTF 2026 writeup
item.description: A deep dive into five advanced forensic, hardware, and cryptographic challenges from V1T CTF 2026: Green Goblin, Nice Try, 10X54, Barely Legal Experience, and XTS-AES.

item.title: V1T CTF 2025 writeup
item.description: A comprehensive technical breakdown of four signature challenges from V1T CTF 2025: 67, Fuck Da Binary, Thirsty Sick, and Tryna crack?. Deep dive into AES bitplane carving, BinaryFuck execution, Scapy packet reassembly, and bkcrack plaintext attacks.
